methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 6 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waymo is a late-stage private autonomous vehicle company in the Drones & Autonomous sector, currently valued at $126B after raising $16B+ in cumulative capital. The addressable comp universe consists of six private peers in the same sector, including Wayve, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, and Archer Aviation. No public comparables exist in this narrow vertical, limiting traditional public-market benchmarking.

The Peer-Median triangulation method is inapplicable to this valuation. While six same-sector peers exist, none of the narrow filters—same-stage private funding round, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier—yielded three or more datapoints necessary for robust median analysis. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneity of business models, commercialization timelines, and capital intensity across the broader autonomous sector.

Given these constraints, this analysis cannot rely on comparable-company triangulation to establish a defensible valuation range. Alternative approaches—discounted cash flow, precedent transaction analysis, or venture-stage methodology—would require additional data not provided. The primary uncertainty is the absence of a sufficiently thick peer group at Waymo's stage and scale. Any valuation conclusion would require either: (1) expansion of the comp set to include adjacent sectors with defensible crossover logic, or (2) application of cash-flow or market-sizing frameworks independent of peer multiples. Current data does not support quantitative range synthesis.
